newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mostly firmer on soybeans.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mostly firmer on soybeans.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended mostly firmer on spillover strength from CBOT soybeans and on renewed concerns about planting delays in the northern U.S. Plains, traders said.
One trader said healthy buying in the September and December contracts was "probably export-related."
"It's been snowing in the Dakotas all day long, and that's caused people to talk about spring flooding and planting delays," MGE trader said.
MGE spring wheat settled one cent per bushel lower to 10 cents higher, with May up 6-1/4 cents at $3.92-1/2 a bushel.
New crop September closed 10 cents higher at $3.82-1/2.
CBOT soybeans surged on fears that a threatened strike at a Brazilian port, called for Wednesday, could spread to other ports across the country and thereby paralyze exports.
MGE barley futures settled five to 10 cents per cwt higher, with March up five cents at $6.70.
